correctness.rationale: For all a,b>=2 and real g>=0, spectral projector compression gives a necessary and sufficient kernel test. For nonunit g a four-dimensional bright invariant block has four distinct nonzero eigenvalues by det B=sqrt(pq)(g-1) and positive BB^T offdiagonal; residual dark blocks are at eigenvalue zero. Dark compression forces all residual coordinates to vanish when cell size >=3, gives one contrast for size 2, and imposes none for size 1. Two bright equations are independent except for balanced a=b>=3, with their determinant factors (q-p)/Delta or (g^2-1)/Delta. The g=1 case is handled independently. Exact rational symmetric-commutant checks for 180 parameter profiles and independent numeric grouped-projector checks for 288 profiles corroborate but cannot prove infinite scope. Boundary g=0, g=1 and a,b=2 are included.

value.rationale: A single bond defect on a complete bipartite quantum transport graph is a natural physical perturbation and the complete nonunit rank law reveals a discontinuous, strength-independent loss of 0, 1, 2 or 3 observable modes. The precise positive-definiteness threshold (unequal part sizes both >=4) and exceptional balanced and size-three boundaries are sharp, nontrivial constraints on robust long-time quantum-network design, not a special-case substitution or an arbitrary parameter slice.
